page.layout: Running head at top centre; page number at top right. Below them, two round coin medallions side by side, each with a legend. Below the medallions, one column of running text in two paragraphs, with the gathering signature at the right after the text. A small woodcut ornament sits at the bottom centre, with no text.

main_text.p: CONSTANS, devicto fratre Constantino, omni conatu superatis Alpibus Galliam intrat, varióq; eventu biennio pugnans, patre fratris in potestatem redigit. Primùm agit bonum principē, mox sive adversa valetudinē, sive rerum prosperitate mutatus, ingratus omnibus esse coepit, donec & ipse Magnentij dolo, quem etiam servaverat, dormiēs[?] intra tentorium, non longe ab Hispaniis, ad Helenam oppidum, opprimitur, anno ætatis 30. Imperij 13. Consulito Pomp. Læt. & Bap. Egna. li.1.

CONSTANTIVS, cædem fratris Constantis ulturus, magno exercitu adversus Magnētium cōparato, ingenti illum prælio, & memorabili, ad Murtiū, sive Mursam, vicit, quo Romani vires Imperij penè cōciderē, 53. millibus utrinque defideratis. Mox cum Magnentius bellū reparasset, & ad Lugdunum iterum victus esset, gladio sibi latus aperuit. Cæterùm Cōstantius, iterum in Persas cōtendens, dum ægrè fert Iulianum à militibus Augustū esse dictum, iuxta Tauri mōtis radices æstuantissima febre correptus, moritur, anno ætatis 40. Imperij 2 4. Hic orbis dominum se vocavit:Iulianum adoptavit. Consulito autores quos supra.

page.notes: Two coin medallions (engravings) at the top, showing laureate busts facing right; their legends are transcribed above as lines. Woodcut ornament at the bottom centre, not transcribed. The "dormiēs" word is uncertain: the tilde over the e is hard to read at this scan resolution. The running head is transcribed with its printed full stop.
